profile.headline: I do cloud, AI, enterprise, embedded, automotive and industrial automation networking. I currently specialize in AI/RDMA, firmware + silicon product design and cybersecurity.
profile.summary:
Currently leading end-to-end system software architecture for NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion program. Responsible for the definition and execution of NVLink Fusion–based product software, including compute tray control plane software, firmware, and interactions with the NVSwitch fabric software. Scope spans user-mode and kernel-mode SDK software, firmware, manufacturing and diagnostics tools.

Previously led the Intel software, firmware and security product architecture for several flagship Ethernet designs, driving cybersecurity response across a virtual organization of ~100 engineers covering 300+ active programs. Prior to that, managed a team of 11 software architects delivering the Intel IPU E2100 software product architecture for LAN, RDMA, NVMe, cryptographic accelerators and cloud infrastructure acceleration services. Earlier, led product architecture, development, validation and release of several generations of Intel Ethernet network interface adapters from inception to end-of-life.

Proven ability to drive innovation at the silicon, system, firmware and software levels and own end-to-end development from initial concept to production deployment. Examples include the Intel IPU E2100; the Intel I210 Ethernet controller (30M+ units/year into automotive IVI, robotics and industrial Ethernet via IEEE 802.1AS/PTP and the AVNu OpenAVB project); MACSec (802.1AE), 802.1X, secure boot and firmware digital signatures (Intel was first to ship signed Ethernet adapter firmware, now required by NIST SP800-193); and Energy Efficient Ethernet integration, including authoring the networking section of the ECMA-393 Network Proxy standard adopted by the US DOE Energy Star program.

Awarded 13 patents covering a range of networking technologies.

positions.title: Principal Engineer
positions.description:
Led and delivered the Intel firmware and security product architecture for an AI-optimized Ethernet SuperNIC design. 

Led cybersecurity response through a virtual organization of approximately one hundred team members for security design and response and over three hundred active programs. Reviewed and approved product security architecture, design and PSIRT response. 

Previous to that, directly managed a team of 11 software architects to deliver the Intel IPU E2100 software product architecture for LAN, RDMA, NVMe, Cryptographic Accelerators and cloud infrastructure acceleration services. 

Previous to that, led and delivered the product architecture design, development, validation and product release of several generations of Intel Ethernet network interface adapter products - from product inception to end-of-life.

Cybersecurity: Defined and delivered into release 802.1AE (MACSec), 802.1X, malicious entity detection and containment, secure boot and firmware digital signatures. Intel was first into the Ethernet adapter market with firmware digital signatures, which is now required by NIST SP800-193.
Time Sensitive Networking: Introduced IEEE 802.1AS / PTP support into the Intel product line and drove software enabling in the Linux kernel and broader ecosystem via the AVNu OpenAVB project. This directly led to sales of 30+ million units per year of Intel I210 Ethernet controllers into automobile in-vehicle-infotainment (IVI) systems, robotics applications and industrial Ethernet applications.
Power Management: Drove definition and integration of Energy Efficient Ethernet into the Intel product line and wrote the networking section of the international ECMA-393 Network Proxy standard, later adopted by the US Department of Energy “Energy Star” program, which enabled Intel platforms to meet the more stringent government requirements.
